added_provisions.reason: Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) carries a proviso letting the parties dispense with the search in writing. The map stated the search duty (PROV-M032-001) as absolute and indispensable without its exception, which check 4 of the verifier prompt exists to catch.

Claim CL-M032-Q01-029 and the gold answer assert that two witnesses must sign. That requirement is rule (8); the map cited only rule (9), which governs identification and the repute of witnesses, not their number.
The gold answer asserts a reading-over and explanation step. Rule (11) is the provision that imposes it, and it does so conditionally; no provision in the map supported the step.
Claim CL-M032-Q01-007 asserts that a priority notice back-dates registration. PROV-M032-016 (s.30(5)) gives only the six-week currency; the relation-back is s.30(2).

Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(2)(a) requires the transferee as well as the transferor to sign and affix a thumb impression on a transfer deed. On a matter whose whole point is advising the buyer, this is indispensable and the map recorded only s.2(1)(a).

Claim CL-M032-Q01-015 asserts that land held above the ceiling vests in the Commission. s.3(2) does that only for land held in excess at the 1972 commencement; for a post-commencement purchaser the vesting provision is s.5(1).

question_decisions.note: Kept as proposed_gold. Every excerpt in the map is verbatim, every rule claim now rests on a recorded provision, no indispensable provision is rejected or unresolved, and the answer cites no case law. Six provisions were added and eleven existing ones downgraded to partially_verified or unresolved, all on stated grounds. statute_only survives on the prompt's test, since the gaps are conveyancing practice rather than case law or Roman-Dutch doctrine, but that judgement is recorded as a disagreement below because the practice steps would carry marks in the original exam.

disagreements.researcher_position: authority_requirement is statute_only because every step in the gold answer is tied to a recorded provision, with the thirty-year title search, non-vesting certificate, street line and building line certificates and rates receipts listed as corpus gaps rather than asserted.
disagreements.verifier_position: The claims as written are statute-supported, so statute_only is defensible on the prompt's own test. But the question asks what steps the notary should take, and a complete practitioner answer would include the non-statutory conveyancing steps the map has parked in corpus_gaps. Marking the item statute_only risks a gold answer that scores well against the corpus and short against the paper.

disagreements.researcher_position: The consolidated section 31 and Prevention of Frauds section 2 texts may be post-2024, but every point relied on predates 2024, so the excerpts were kept as cut.
disagreements.verifier_position: Agreed on substance, but the wording actually quoted for PROV-M032-002 and PROV-M032-007 sits in runs that the corpus attributes to substitutions by Act No. 6 of 2024, and the corpus records no commencement date. For an April 2024 matter the quoted wording, not just the substance, should be settled before the excerpts are used as gold.

unsupported_claims: CL-M032-Q01-007: 'back-dates the registration ... to the date of the notice' was not in the cited excerpt (s.30(5)); resolved by adding PROV-M032-904 (s.30(2)).

CL-M032-Q01-015: 'land owned in excess of that ceiling vests in the Commission' was not in the cited excerpt (s.3(1)(b)) and s.3(2) does not reach a post-1972 purchaser; resolved by adding PROV-M032-906 (s.5(1)).

CL-M032-Q01-029: the two-witness requirement and the reading-over step had no supporting provision; resolved by adding PROV-M032-902 (rule (8)) and PROV-M032-903 (rule (11)). Note that rule (11) is conditional, so the claim's flat 'read over and explain the deed' remains wider than the rule.
CL-M032-Q01-029 also asserted that the notary identifies both parties without any provision requiring the buyer to be on the deed; PROV-M032-905 (Prevention of Frauds s.2(2)(a)) now supplies that.
temporal_issues: PROV-M032-020 (Notaries Ordinance s.38A) is in_force_from_year 2024 with no commencement date in the corpus; marked unresolved. It is supporting only, and claim CL-M032-Q01-018 is marked disputed because it turns on it.

PROV-M032-002 and PROV-M032-007 quote wording inside runs of section 31 that the corpus attributes to Act No. 6 of 2024; the corpus records years only, so the April 2024 wording cannot be confirmed. Both marked partially_verified.
PROV-M032-013 quotes Prevention of Frauds s.2(1)(a) as consolidated after Act No. 4 of 2024; same year-only limitation. Marked partially_verified.
PROV-M032-017: the ceiling is unchanged since 1981, but the vesting consequence the claim relied on is time-limited to the 1972 commencement. Corrected by PROV-M032-906.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) proviso (written dispensation of the search) was missing; added as PROV-M032-901 with an 'excepts' edge to PROV-M032-001.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (30A) proviso (sixty days where the deed must be registered outside the notary's jurisdiction) was not recorded; it does not bite here because the land and the notary are both in Kurunegala. PROV-M032-010 marked partially_verified and the point noted there.
Prevention of Frauds s.2(1)(b) (thumb impressions of every executant) and s.2(2)(a) (transferee must sign) were missing; s.2(2)(a) added as PROV-M032-905.

Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act s.3(4) requires the consent certificate to be attached to the deed and the fact stated in the attestation. The map records only s.3(1)(a); since the finding is that coconut is outside the Act, nothing turns on it, but claim CL-M032-Q01-017's reference to attachment rests on s.3(4).
Land Development Ordinance s.19(7) (no approval needed to mortgage to a licensed commercial bank) was checked and is not engaged on these facts.
Land Reform Law s.13 (reporting alienations to the Commission) was checked: it is a 1972 transitional reporting duty running three months from commencement and creates no step for a 2024 conveyance.
case_law_dependence: None found. No claim, issue or part of the gold answer draft cites a decided case, and the validator's case-law regex is clean. The non-statutory material the answer would otherwise need (thirty-year title chain, non-vesting certificate, rates and street line certificates) is conveyancing practice, not judicial authority.
enrichment_issues: No leak found: the enriched background names no Act, no section number and states no conclusion. The vendor, land, plan, bond and price are ordinary conveyancing facts.

Every synthetic_decisive fact carries a reason and a counterfactual. FACT-M032-Q01-004 (the bank bond) is acceptable: it creates something for the search to disclose without deciding the legal issue, since the answer is the same set of steps either way.

FACT-M032-Q01-006 bundles two unrelated facts (the intended execution date and the notary's authorised area and language) into one fact entry; they activate different provisions and would be cleaner split. Not corrected here because it does not affect support.
The legal issue is unchanged by the enrichment: the question remains what steps the notary must take on a purchase of the estate.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: No duplicate provision ids, and the indispensable, supporting and background sets remain disjoint after the additions.

Twelve of the twenty-seven provisions are separate rules of the single section 1-1907/s31. That is legitimate, but a scorer that counts distinct sections rather than distinct provisions will read this matter as resting on far fewer authorities than the map suggests.

lawyer_questions: Is a statute_only gold answer acceptable for a 'what steps should the notary take' question when the thirty-year title search, the non-vesting certificate and the rates and street line certificates - the steps that would carry marks in the original paper - are professional practice with no provision in the corpus? If not, M032-Q01 should be reserved rather than proposed_gold.

Were the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024 and the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 4 of 2024 in force by April 2024? The corpus records years only, which leaves the exact wording quoted for PROV-M032-002, PROV-M032-007, PROV-M032-013 and the whole of PROV-M032-020 unsettled.
